We contrast the queried attribute, state, event, count, or temporal relationship. Backgrounds, viewpoints, and unrelated objects are matched as closely as the source material permits; the recent frames are identical.

Every pair, question, and answer key receives human review after automatic and AI-assisted checks. Residual differences can remain in the histories. The boxes above highlight the queried region; they are not exact editing masks.

    Why test historical evidence separately?+

    Recent frames may already give the answer.

    In an additional audit of OVO-Bench and StreamingBench, recent frames suffice for 32% of 400 sampled historical questions.

    The question itself can suggest an answer.

    With no visual input, Qwen3-VL-8B and DeepSeek-Flash reach 40.83% and 49.60% accuracy on the same 4,276 questions across the two benchmarks.

    TwinPast fixes the recent view and the question. Repeating an answer favored by this shared information cannot solve both histories.

    Paper §3. The 32% describes the additional historical-task sample, not either benchmark as a whole. The text-only figures cover the full evaluated question set.

    What model errors reveal+

    Retaining evidence does not guarantee its correct use.

    These paper case studies show why time references, event order, counts, and combinations of facts also matter.

    REKV · SELECTING THE QUERIED STATE

    The right states.
    The wrong moment.

    All eight sampled frames per branch remain available, including both door states. The question asks for the state at the end of the first kitchen shot.

    Initial stateQueried final state
    01Open→Closed
    02Closed→Open

    Model answers: Open / Closed Both reversed

    Keeping the states available does not ensure selection of the state at the requested time.

    ONESTREAMER · USING RECORDED ORDER

    The order is recorded.
    The answer contradicts it.

    The memory supplied to the final question records both events and their order.

    2–7 sSpray bottle placed in the box
    7–10 sHairbrush placed in the box

    Model selects: Hairbrush first

    Answering correctly also requires using the temporal relationships expressed in memory.

    COUNTS & COMBINATIONS

    Every occurrence.
    Every relevant fact.

    The best task PairAcc among evaluated streaming systems is 15.8% for action counting and 25.4% for multi-event integration (Figure 3).

    In 13 of 46 multi-event pairs combining two binary facts, AURA answers one fact correctly in both branches while repeating the other, even though both facts change. A different option can still reflect an incomplete response to history.

    These case studies illustrate specific failure modes. A failed pair by itself does not establish whether evidence was missed, forgotten, or used incorrectly.

    Within the Qwen3.8-Omni family, PairAcc is 49.14% for the realtime variant versus 82.86% for its non-realtime counterpart. They produce different valid answers on 57.14% and 89.14% of pairs respectively. These are the evaluated variants and protocols, not a controlled comparison of architecture alone.

    Dataset scope and sources+

    The 350 human-reviewed pairs cover attribute and identity recall (92), historical states (77), event order (65), action counting (57), and multi-event integration (59).

    Source material comes from MVP, DyBench, ReCo-Data, DualityVidQA, VidPair-Halluc, and Perception Test.

    Evaluation targets historical questions at specified query times. It does not measure proactive response timing or latency. Spliced histories and shared source material can retain unrelated visual differences; temporal annotations vary in precision. Evidence-acquisition and delay studies need to verify the evidence supplied to each system.
